lines:
Implemented in commit dd70fa2, pushed to origin/main.

**What shipped.** A new read-only task-list control in the composer, immediately left of the goal button (`ChatComposer` gained a `todoControl` slot rendered before `{goalControl}`, wired in `ChatWorkspaceScreen` beside `GoalControl`). New files `TodoControl.tsx`, `todo.css` and `todoProjection.ts`; `ChatComposer.tsx` itself grew by only the slot prop.

**Data is parsed once.** `todoProjection.todosFromFact` is the single parser, and `currentTodos(events)` folds the newest `tool.todo` fact in one pass without copying the stream. Both existing readers were moved onto it: `activityProjection.todoCard`'s body and `ConversationTimeline.todosOf`, which is now a thin done/active adapter. That satisfies acceptance criterion 7 and removes the second, subtly different status mapping that treated "done" as completed only on the timeline side.

**Acceptance criteria.** (1) the button is present with and without a list; (2) clicking opens a `role="dialog"` with every entry, its status label and an "N of M done" count, and a second click or Escape closes it; (3) a chat with no `tool.todo` fact shows "This Chat has no task list yet."; (4) a newer fact updates the open dialog without a reload and without remounting the composer, asserted by rerendering with an added event; (5) read-only — no editing affordance and no command dispatched; (6) the trigger is keyboard reachable, has a tooltip built from the progress, sets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and focus returns to it on Escape; (7) one parser, shared.

**Judgement calls worth knowing.** An unknown or missing status counts as pending, the only safe reading of unfinished work (tested). Escape and pointer dismissal differ on purpose: Escape restores focus to the trigger, an outside click does not steal it. Empty list and no list share the empty state, since both mean there is nothing to inspect.

**Verification.** `npx vitest run src/chat src/workbench` 57 files / 442 tests passed; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vite build` succeeded. I deliberately did not run `prettier --write` over the four edited files: they are already non-conforming at HEAD (the repository has a large formatting baseline), so formatting them whole would have added unrelated churn. My added lines are prettier-conformant except one prop line in `ChatWorkspaceScreen.tsx`, which stays at the surrounding block's existing indentation rather than becoming the single correctly indented line in an already-dirty block.

## Why

The first DSH vs Aworkit benchmark (same prompt, same model) showed the two harnesses handle the agent's task list in opposite, both-unsatisfying ways.

* **DSH** showed the list in its UI while the run was going, but the state went stale and was wrong at the end. It wrote the list twice and never again: sequence 32 at 10:33:18 and sequence 129 at 10:35:57, while the run continued until 10:44:42. The state the UI left on screen was:
  ```
  [completed  ] Write src/engine.js (pure rules engine, UMD)
  [completed  ] Find seed+plan constructions for 1/2/3/4-line clears offline
  [in_progress] Write src/render.js, src/input.js, src/main.js, index.html, styles.css
  [pending    ] Write selfcheck.js with >=25 assertions and iterate to pass
  [pending    ] Write README.md documenting rules and kick table
  [pending    ] Verify in Firefox (file://) renders and no console errors
  ```
  Every one of those items was in fact finished (all eight files written, `node selfcheck.js` reporting 152/152, Firefox verified, README written), so the visible list was wrong for the last nine minutes.
* **Aworkit** had the correct data but no live view. Its single `tool.todo` call happened at the very end of the run (sequence 10566, 10:46:55) with every entry correctly marked, so during the run there was nothing to look at. The timeline already renders a task card (`activityProjection.ts` `todoCard`, `ConversationTimeline.tsx`), but that card only exists once the agent writes the list.

The lesson for Aworkit is not the agent's discipline, it is that the latest known list must be inspectable at any moment of a run, whether or not the agent happened to write it recently.

## What to build

Give the Chat a persistent task-list control that mirrors the existing goal control: an icon button in the composer immediately left of the goal flag button. Clicking it opens a read-only popover showing the state of the list, or an explicit empty state when the Chat has no list yet.

## Where

* Composer toolbar slot: `desktop/src/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:311`, the `composer-submit-controls` row currently ordered `subagentsControl`, `goalControl`, `contextUsage`. Add a `todoControl?: React.ReactNode` prop beside `goalControl` (declared at `ChatComposer.tsx:27`) and render it immediately before `{goalControl}`.
* Wiring: `desktop/src/chat/ChatWorkspaceScreen.tsx:803`, beside the existing `goalControl={<GoalControl events={runtime.events} …/>}`.
* Pattern to mirror: `desktop/src/chat/GoalControl.tsx` (175 lines) with its styles in `desktop/src/chat/goal.css`. The goal button is `.goal-flag-button` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`; the popover is `role="dialog"` with `.goal-popover`. The goal is editable, the task list must not be.
* New files: `desktop/src/chat/TodoControl.tsx` and `desktop/src/chat/todo.css`. Do not grow `ChatComposer.tsx` beyond the new slot prop.

## Data

Source is the newest `tool.todo` event for the Chat (`payload.todos`, entries of `{content, status}` with `status` one of `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`). Reuse the extraction that already feeds the timeline card (`activityProjection.ts` `todoCard` and the `todosOf` helper in `ConversationTimeline.tsx`) rather than parsing the payload a second time, so the button and the card can never disagree.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The button is present in the composer at all times, immediately left of the goal button, both for a Chat that has a list and for one that does not.
2. Clicking it opens a dialog listing every entry with its status and a completed/total count; clicking it again, or pressing Escape, closes it and returns focus to the button.
3. A Chat with no `tool.todo` event shows an explicit empty state instead of an empty box.
4. The popover reflects a newer `tool.todo` event that arrives while the run is still going, without a page reload and without remounting the composer.
5. Read-only: there is no editing affordance and no command is dispatched on open, close or inspection.
6. Accessible: the button is keyboard reachable, carries a tooltip, sets `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`, and points `aria-controls` at the popover id.
7. The task list is parsed in exactly one place; the timeline card and this control share it.

## Tests

* A component test beside `GoalControl.test.tsx` covering: the empty state, statuses rendered for all three values, a live update when a newer `tool.todo` event arrives, and keyboard open/close with focus return.
* Extend the existing projection test if the shared extraction changes.

## Related observation, decide separately

Aworkit's agent wrote its list once, at the very end, as a closing summary. `tool.todo`'s manifest instructions already say "Keep it current and mark items complete only after their work is done", so the guidance exists; if the list should read as a live plan rather than a closing report, the DSH Standard workflow's Agent instructions would need to say so. That is a workflow change, not part of this UI task.

data.title: Show the agent's task list in the composer, left of the goal control
